$comment: Static-analysis findings a person has read and accepted as not defects, honoured by
scripts/sarif-gate.py in the CodeQL and Trivy jobs of .github/workflows/ci.yml.
This is not a way to stop seeing a finding. An accepted finding is still listed in the job
summary, with the reason below beside it, so a reviewer sees what the gate did not stop on. What
the entry removes is the build failure, and only for the exact finding it describes.
Matching is on the rule, the file and a fragment of the message - never on a line number, which
moves with the next edit above it, and never on the file alone. A different finding of the same
rule in the same file is a different finding and fails the build until somebody reads it too.
An entry that matches nothing fails the build. That is the dangerous state: the finding it
described has been fixed or has changed, so the register would otherwise be accepting something
nobody has read. Remove the entry, or read the finding again.
There is a third cause, and it cost an afternoon on 2026-09-07, so it is written down. The CodeQL
C# job runs with build-mode 'none': the source is extracted without a build, and the NuGet and
dotnet CLIs only contribute information about external dependencies. Which external methods are
modelled as taint sinks therefore moves with the dependency set - so a dependency bump can make a
finding appear or disappear with no change to a single line of this repository's code. That is what
happened to the two cs/cleartext-storage-of-sensitive-information entries below: they were removed
on 2026-09-07 as stale, and on 2026-09-09 a later bump produced both findings again, against a
SessionService.cs and two PasswordChanged enum members that had not changed a byte in between. They
are restored with the reading they were accepted under, because that reading is still the right one.
So: before removing an entry, check whether the code it names actually changed; if it did not, say
so where the removal is recorded and keep the reason, because the next bump may well want it again.
`scope` names the scan the entry belongs to, and the gate is given a --scope so it applies only
the entries written for the run in hand. It is not decoration: the CodeQL job is a matrix over
csharp and javascript-typescript, and without it a C# entry matches nothing on the JavaScript run
and fails it as stale - which is what happened the first time this was wired in.
The same field is what will let a Trivy finding live here beside a CodeQL one.
This register is for findings that are wrong. A finding that is right but is being carried
anyway is a different thing and belongs in docs/process/waivers.md, with an owner and an expiry.

accepted.reason: The value logged is the enum member SessionRotationReason.PasswordChanged — a reason code, not a credential. CodeQL's heuristic reads the identifier, sees 'Password', and treats the constant as sensitive data reaching a log sink. What the line actually writes is 'Rotated session X into Y because PasswordChanged', which is the audit trail this rotation exists to leave. Removed on 2026-09-07 when a dependency bump stopped the scanner producing it, and restored on 2026-09-09 when the next bump brought it back against byte-identical code; the reason it was not a defect has not changed, so it is the same reading, not a new one.

The same heuristic on the same word, one type along: SessionEndReason.PasswordChanged is the reason every other session was revoked when somebody changed their password. The enum is persisted by name (IdentityDbContext maps it with HasConversion<string>), so the member is a stored reason code; renaming it to something without the word 'password' would be a data migration made to satisfy a scanner, and would make the vocabulary worse. Removed on 2026-09-07 when a dependency bump stopped the scanner producing it, and restored on 2026-09-09 when the next bump brought it back against byte-identical code; the reason it was not a defect has not changed, so it is the same reading, not a new one.
